entities.name: Áed mac Colggen
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Áed mac Colggen was a king of the Uí Cheinnselaig of Leinster, a prominent dynasty of medieval Ireland whose sovereignty and dynastic succession shaped the political landscape of Leinster during the eighth century. Some sources incorrectly make him joint king of Leinster with Bran Becc mac Murchada, but it appears that Áed was the main ruler of Leinster in 738, wielding sovereign authority during a period of significant feudal governance and interplay between religious and secular power structures.

Aéd was the son of Colcú mac Bressail, who was called king of Ard Ladrann at his death, according to an obit recorded in the annals in 722 which noted that he was killed. This lineage connected Áed to a distinguished royal pedigree—he was the great-great grandson of Crundmáel Erbuilc, a previous King of Leinster, and was a member of the Sil Chormaic sept, a branch of the Uí Cheinnselaig dynasty known for maintaining territorial boundaries and dynastic legacies across generations.

Áed mac Colggen died on August 23, 738, leaving behind an established legacy that contributed to the synthesis of classical governance traditions and religious authority that characterized the Medieval era. His rule exemplified the complex interplay of monarchical power, feudal obligations, and the dynastic succession traditions that would influence European political systems for centuries to come.
